newsitem.title: TAIWAN: E.Asia Oilseeds - USDA report seen key for soy.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - USDA report seen key for soy.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) stocks and acreage report due out later on Monday is expected to be bearish for nearby July Chicago soybean contracts but support forward positions, East Asia traders said. Taiwanese traders said they expected the USDA report to show a reduction in the planting acreage for soybeans and a drop in quarterly sobyean stocks.
"The USDA report will affect the new soybean crops, but the July is still bearish," a trader said.
The July CBOT soybean contract dropped 13-1/4 U.S. cents per bushel on Friday,

A South Korean trader said the recent narrowing spread between the old crop and new crop in soybean prices would absorb any impact of the USDA report even though U.S. old crop inventory had declined to near 20-year lows.

"The spread between the old and new crop has been narrowed to about $1.40 a bushel over the new crop from its previous $1.80 to $1.90 in April and May due to the bearish mood helped by weak export figures and good weather in the United States," the trader said.
"The grain and oilseed markets will fall further unless there is fundamental news which can reverse the current bearish trend," he added.
Japanese buyers said they would continue to wait for the expected lower-priced soybean crop from October before entering the market.
"Although the backwardation narrowed recently, that's not enough to attract us," a soybean trader in Tokyo said.
Taiwanese buyers said they too are waiting for soy futures to bottom out before re-entering the market.
"Its hard to say how far soybean and corn futures can fall," one buyer said.

South Korean feed millers and crushers are expected to continue covering their requirements for soybeans, soymeal and other meals this week, encouraged by the recent sharp declines in world prices, traders said.
"We expect several buyers to buy about 30,000 tonnes of soymeal and 15,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal for arrival in October," a trader with a local feed miller said.
But the trader said the National Livestock Cooperatives Federation's (NLCF) was seen continuing to delay its plan to buy soymeal and other meals.

The NLCF has been seeking 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for October 20 arrival, 30,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellet for arrival between November and December and 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal for arrival in December.
